title: Best Krav Maga Software: Prices & Level Tracking (2026)
description: Krav Maga school software compared: Kicksite, Zen Planner, Spark, Dojo Champ, Martialytics and Gymdesk on level tracking, seminars and published prices.
body:
A Krav Maga school usually mixes regular memberships with self-defense seminars and corporate workshops, tracks practitioner levels (not always belts), and often runs women's self-defense or law-enforcement specialty classes alongside beginner and advanced groups. This page compares six tools on what each vendor says about Krav Maga and on its published prices, checked November 7, 2026. Kicksite, Zen Planner and Spark Membership each have a page written specifically for Krav Maga schools; for Dojo Champ, Martialytics and Gymdesk we found no dedicated Krav Maga product page, so treat those three as general martial arts tools.

{{table:kicksite,zen-planner,spark-membership,dojo-champ,martialytics,gymdesk}}

What each vendor says about Krav Maga

  • Kicksite has a dedicated Krav Maga gym software page. It lists recurring membership billing, one-time charges and inventory for merch, kiosk check-in by name, PIN or barcode with mass check-in and past-due or unsigned-waiver restrictions, customizable belt ranks tied to programs (for schools that use a Krav Maga belt system or also run Jiu-Jitsu), free unlimited one-way texts and emails, lead capture forms and landing pages that can sell trials or memberships online. Its homepage and FAQ also name Krav Maga among the school types it serves. Pricing on that page matches the main pricing page: $49–$199/mo by active student count.
  • Zen Planner has a Krav Maga school management page. It says built-in skill tracking manages practitioner levels, instructor certifications and skill progressions, with automated alerts for who is ready to advance; you can set up beginner, advanced, women's self-defense, law enforcement and specialty classes with distinct pricing and schedules; and automated billing, lead follow-ups and member communications run in the background. Its FAQ on that page says pricing starts at $99/mo and scales by active members (prospects and staff not charged).
  • Spark Membership's Krav Maga gym software page says Krav Maga schools attract regular members plus corporate groups and one-off seminar attendees, and that Spark handles level and attendance tracking, seminar and corporate self-defense workshop bookings, automatic billing with failed-payment recovery, two-way SMS for new leads, and real-time reporting for memberships and seminars in one CRM. The page says Spark was built by two 7th Dan black belts who ran martial arts schools. Pricing stated on the page is an 8-week free trial, then $199/mo, with free student data migration.
  • Dojo Champ publishes a Krav Maga schools directory style listing, but we found no dedicated Krav Maga product page. Its martial arts school software page lists built-in rank systems for karate, taekwondo, BJJ, judo, kung fu and Kajukenbo plus custom belt orders, attendance, recurring tuition and a flat $199/mo plan with unlimited students. A Krav Maga school can still set up a custom level system, but ask for a demo with your progression model before committing.
  • Martialytics and Gymdesk don't have a Krav Maga product page on the sites we checked. Martialytics publishes martial arts pricing from $69/mo and lists features such as grading-readiness tracking, kiosk check-in and bookings; its blog posts discuss Krav Maga as a discipline but do not claim product features for Krav Maga schools. Gymdesk's martial arts software page covers attendance, promotions, payments and bookings, and a Gymdesk blog post on martial arts types includes a Krav Maga section noting memberships plus workshops/corporate training as a common business mix. Some public Gymdesk-hosted school sites are Krav Maga academies, but that is not the same as a vendor Krav Maga claim.

Small school (under 50 members)

Kicksite has the lowest published price at $49/mo for 0-25 students ($99 for 26-50). Martialytics is $69/mo for up to 50 students and Gymdesk is $75/mo for up to 50 active members with Gymdesk Payments ($100/mo with your own processor). If practitioner-level tracking plus specialty class pricing is the deciding feature, Zen Planner is the one with those claims on a dedicated Krav Maga page, starting from $99/mo. {{aff:kicksite|Visit Kicksite}}

Schools that run seminars and corporate workshops

Spark Membership is the only vendor here that says on its Krav Maga page that self-defense seminars and corporate workshops share the same checkout and calendar as regular memberships, with reporting that shows both revenue streams. Zen Planner's Krav Maga page lists women's self-defense, law enforcement and specialty classes with their own schedules and pricing. Kicksite's Krav Maga page lists landing pages that can sell trials or memberships online. {{aff:sparkmembership|Visit Spark Membership}} · {{aff:zenplanner|Visit Zen Planner}}

Growing school (100-200 members)

Martialytics is $129/mo for 101-200 students with every feature, unlimited users and locations. Kicksite is $199/mo for 101+. Gymdesk is $150/mo (101-150) or $200/mo (151-250) with Gymdesk Payments. Dojo Champ and Spark each list a single $199/mo price. Zen Planner Studio is $229/mo for 101-150 active members or $239/mo for 151-200 (Zen Planner tiers, checked 2026-11-09). {{aff:martialytics|Visit Martialytics}} · {{aff:dojochamp|Visit Dojo Champ}}

faq: Is there software made specifically for Krav Maga schools?

Not that we found as a Krav Maga-only product. Kicksite, Zen Planner and Spark Membership each have a page written for Krav Maga gyms or schools, but all of them are general martial arts platforms. We found no dedicated Krav Maga product page for Dojo Champ, Martialytics or Gymdesk.
Can the software track practitioner levels instead of belts?

Zen Planner's Krav Maga page says skill tracking manages practitioner levels, instructor certifications and skill progressions, with automated alerts for who is ready to advance. Spark Membership's Krav Maga page says practitioner levels are tied to attendance data in one profile. Kicksite's Krav Maga page says customizable belt ranks work if your school uses a belt system. Ask for a demo with your own level names before committing.
Which tools handle self-defense seminars and corporate workshops?

Spark Membership's Krav Maga page says you can sell and manage one-off seminars and corporate self-defense workshops through the same checkout and calendar as regular memberships, with reporting that shows both. Zen Planner's Krav Maga page lists women's self-defense, law enforcement and specialty classes with distinct pricing and schedules.
What is the cheapest option for a small Krav Maga school?

Of the published prices we checked on November 7, 2026, Kicksite starts at $49/mo for 0-25 students, Martialytics at $69/mo for up to 50 students, and Gymdesk at $75/mo for up to 50 active members with Gymdesk Payments ($100/mo with your own processor). Zen Planner starts from $99/mo and Spark and Dojo Champ list $199/mo. Martialytics, Gymdesk and Dojo Champ don't have a dedicated Krav Maga product page on the sites we checked.
Do these tools have free trials?

Martialytics and Gymdesk offer 30 days with no credit card, Kicksite says your first 30 days are free, Dojo Champ offers 30 days with a card required (first charge on day 31 if not cancelled), and Spark Membership offers 8 weeks. We couldn't find a published free trial for Zen Planner.
